- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show >+2% above true outcome, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days); reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3+ consecutive increases), model often fails to adjust for volatility; add 0.5–1.0% downward buffer for next 3–5 days.
